context.stem: A photographer edits a RAW image with severely clipped highlights in a sunset sky and crushed shadows in the foreground rocks. The histogram shows data touching both edges. Which processing sequence maximizes recoverable detail while minimizing artifacts?

choices.text: First reduce exposure to recover highlight data, then lift shadows with a tone curve that avoids excessive local contrast
Apply aggressive shadow recovery first to reveal detail, then pull back highlights with recovery slider
Increase overall contrast to stretch the midtones and hide the clipping
Convert to JPEG first for smaller file size, then apply shadow and highlight adjustments

evidence.name: Adobe: Introduction to Camera Raw
evidence.text: Source: https://helpx.adobe.com/camera-raw/desktop/get-started/overview-and-setup/introduction-camera-raw.html (accessed 2026-09-06). Paraphrase: Camera Raw retains the original raw image data. It records adjustment settings as metadata in a database, sidecar file, or DNG. A Bridge preview is a JPEG rendered using current settings, rather than the raw samples themselves.

evidence.name: Adobe: Develop module adjustments
evidence.text: Source: https://helpx.adobe.com/lightroom-classic/desktop/help/applying-adjustments-develop-module-basic.html (accessed 2026-09-06). Paraphrase: Lightroom Classic Develop edits are nondestructive. The user may make panel adjustments in any order; working from top to bottom is a common approach.

evidence.name: Adobe: Camera Raw color and tone
evidence.text: Source: https://helpx.adobe.com/camera-raw/desktop/using/make-color-tonal-adjustments-camera.html (accessed 2026-09-06). Paraphrase: Clipping in an output representation loses detail beyond its representable range. Exposure adjusts overall brightness; Highlights adjusts bright regions and Shadows adjusts dark regions. The older Recovery control attempts reconstruction where one or two color channels are clipped. The documentation does not guarantee recovery of all captured highlight detail.

context.stem: You need to find all pairs in an unsorted array that sum to target k. Which approach gives O(n) time and O(n) space?

choices.text: Hash map storing complements seen so far
Binary search for each element's complement

evidence.name: Executed pair enumeration examples
evidence.text: Calculation context, not an added premise about the question: arrays of n zeroes, target 0, count each index pair i < j once. A Python itertools.combinations enumeration produced [{"length": 2, "matching_distinct_index_pairs": 1, "pair_exists": true}, {"length": 4, "matching_distinct_index_pairs": 6, "pair_exists": true}, {"length": 8, "matching_distinct_index_pairs": 28, "pair_exists": true}, {"length": 16, "matching_distinct_index_pairs": 120, "pair_exists": true}, {"length": 32, "matching_distinct_index_pairs": 496, "pair_exists": true}]. For each size the count also equals n*(n-1)/2. The Boolean existence result and enumeration output are different quantities. These are finite examples, not a timing benchmark or a proof of an arbitrary implementation.
